items.claim: Q3 2026: Q3 2026 (quarter ended 30 Sep 2026; final results 29 Oct 2026, preliminary 8 Oct 2026): consolidated revenue KRW 195.3 trillion (+14% QoQ, a record) and operating profit KRW 107.4 trillion, which Samsung calls the first time any tech company has passed KRW 100 trillion in quarterly operating profit. DS (chips) revenue KRW 147.1 trillion, operating profit KRW 106.5 trillion, with Memory at all-time highs and HBM4 sales significantly scaled up. DX posted an operating loss of KRW 0.8 trillion (MX/Networks revenue KRW 37.7 trillion, loss KRW 0.6 trillion; VD/DA revenue KRW 13.9 trillion, loss KRW 0.2 trillion). Samsung Display revenue KRW 8.0 trillion, operating profit KRW 1.1 trillion. Against expectations (preliminary figures): operating profit was 0.71% above FnGuide consensus of KRW 106.64 trillion, while revenue missed FnGuide's KRW 200.64 trillion by 2.81%. Prior quarter Q2 2026 (30 Jul 2026): revenue KRW 171.5 trillion, operating profit KRW 89.5 trillion, EPS KRW 10,849.

Q3 2026: If our figures stop at FY2025, both Q2 and Q3 2026 are newer and show quarterly operating profit at KRW 89.5 trillion and KRW 107.4 trillion, almost entirely from chips, so annual figures understate the current earnings level (the briefing links Samsung's results press release and did not confirm whether the full K-IFRS quarterly filing is on DART yet).

Korea Fair Trade Commission decided a tentative fine of about KRW 20 billion (~USD 15.1 million) plus corrective order over Galaxy S21/S22/Tab S8 gaming ads that did not disclose Game Optimizing Service CPU/GPU limits; Samsung contests it.

Seoul High Court cancelled the KFTC's 2021 Welstory in-house catering 'unfair support' corrective order and fine (combined KRW 234.9 billion across affiliates) for insufficient evidence; whether the KFTC appealed to the Supreme Court is unverified.

Separate Welstory criminal case at Seoul Central District Court against former Future Strategy Office head Choi Gee-sung, Samsung Welstory and a former executive (indicted Nov 2022); first trial underway as of Apr 2026, outcome unverified.

Netlist v. Samsung (E.D. Texas / Federal Circuit): juries found willful infringement of memory-module patents ($303 million in Apr 2023, $118 million in Nov 2024); Samsung argued the $303 million damages method was flawed before the Federal Circuit, no decision found.
Texas Attorney General smart-TV ACR lawsuit under the Deceptive Trade Practices Act resolved by agreement: Samsung to update TVs to clearly disclose ACR and obtain consent; no monetary penalty found.
Pictiva Displays / Key Patent Innovations v. Samsung (E.D. Texas): jury found willful infringement of two OLED display patents and awarded $191.4 million; no post-trial or appellate result found.

Collision Communications v. Samsung (E.D. Texas): jury found Galaxy phones and laptops infringed four wireless patents and awarded $445.5 million; permanent injunction denied 18 May 2026; no ruling on post-trial challenge or appeal found.
Maxell v. Samsung (E.D. Texas): $112 million jury verdict set aside; judge granted Samsung judgment as a matter of law of non-infringement on all three patents and invalidity on two.

Supreme Court of Korea upheld the acquittal of Executive Chairman Lee Jae-yong on all 19 charges (stock manipulation, accounting fraud concerning Samsung Biologics, breach of trust) tied to the 2015 Samsung C&T-Cheil merger; Samsung Electronics was not the corporate defendant.

Indian customs authorities ordered Samsung to pay about $601 million (back taxes plus 100% penalty) over alleged misclassification of Remote Radio Head imports sold to Reliance Jio; Samsung India challenged it before CESTAT Mumbai, no decision found.

Korea's Nuclear Safety and Security Commission found Samsung violated the Nuclear Safety Act after X-ray exposure of two workers at the Giheung plant, with three safety interlocks arbitrarily manipulated; fined and ordered corrective measures.
Federal Court of Australia ordered Samsung Electronics Australia to pay A$14 million (ACCC case) after it admitted misleading consumers about water resistance of seven Galaxy models.

Seoul High Court retrial sentenced then Vice Chairman Lee Jae-yong to 2 years 6 months for bribes of about KRW 8.6 billion to then-President Park Geun-hye via Choi Soon-sil, using embezzled company funds; sentence became final.
European Commission DRAM cartel settlement decision fined nine producers EUR 331 million combined; Samsung fined EUR 145,728,000 after leniency and settlement reductions.
US Department of Justice: Samsung Electronics and its US subsidiary agreed to plead guilty and pay a $300 million criminal fine for DRAM price-fixing from April 1999 to June 2002.
